headline: Day one of the 580 km crossing. The taper landed clean and the engine is banked. From here the trail is the only data that counts.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The build into this start was deliberate and it held together: the four-week running block ran meaningfully higher than the prior block, strength stayed live right to the edge with short, sharp sessions in the final week, and background step volume has been sitting high enough to add real time-on-feet before the pack even goes on. The taper trimmed load without hollowing anything out — the recent easy runs sit comfortably in the aerobic zones, nothing forced. The DETRAINING flag on cardio load is an artifact of the deliberate pre-event wind-down, not a fitness signal; treat it as noise this week. What matters now shifts entirely: the question stops being what the training says and becomes how the body absorbs consecutive loaded days under a pack.
sections.trends: The year-to-date picture is unambiguous — distance run to date sits far ahead of the same point last year, and the recent four-week block built on the one before it rather than coasting. That shape makes sense for someone walking into a multi-day crossing: a genuine build, then a clean pull-back into the start. The 12-week average masks how much of that volume is quality durability work rather than junk miles. This is not a plateau or an irregular stretch — it's a build-then-taper arc executed to plan.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace has held flat across the last month, which during a taper is exactly what you want to see — no erosion, no forced sharpening. The engine that produced the recent long efforts is intact and rested. For the crossing itself, threshold is almost irrelevant to the pace you'll actually hold; the relevant capacity is sustained low-aerobic output repeated day after day, and the banked threshold fitness simply means that steady effort will cost less than it otherwise would.
sections.zones: The recent session shapes tell the real story better than any weekly aggregate: the final taper runs sat almost entirely in Z1–Z2 with low maxes, genuinely easy rather than easy-on-average. Step back two weeks and the long run showed real Z3–Z4 time — a proper hard effort — while the mid-length runs held a controlled Z2 base. That's a clean separation between hard and easy days, which is precisely the distribution you want heading into an effort where discipline over pace, not intensity, decides how the back half goes.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions continue to sit low and steady in the aerobic zones, consistent with functional circuit work rather than max-strength grinding — no HR surprises there. Where run HR and effort estimates overlap, the picture is internally consistent, so nothing about the sensor sourcing changes how the recent efforts should be read.
sections.calendar: The running streak is at its all-time best and strength has held an unbroken run of weeks alongside it — but the more telling thing is the pairing: strength stayed on the calendar right into the final taper days rather than being dropped early. That's the habit that keeps the frame durable under a loaded pack, and it's the kind of consistency that matters far more over a nine-day crossing than any single session.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current PBs are in play this week — the focus is entirely on the opposite end of the spectrum. Worth noting the longest-distance record was set on a 137 km effort; the crossing ahead dwarfs that in cumulative terms, and the durability you build over the coming days will quietly reshape what's realistic at the ultra end of your range later.

watch_items: Watch how easy-effort HR recalibrates over the first loaded days — the pack and consecutive terrain will reset your sense of what steady costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability, not the aerobic engine, is the genuine unknown here.
Read the border mountain crossing as its own terrain spike, distinct from the flatter coastal sections.
Watch whether nightly recovery settles once trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.
